/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field with a stable first-order theory
is separably closed. Here the first-order theory of a field $K$ is its complete theory
$\mathrm{Th}(K)$ in the language of rings $\{+, \cdot, -, 0, 1\}$.

Mathlib does not define stability of a first-order theory, so it is defined here. A theory $T$
is *stable* if no formula has the order property in $T$, i.e. there are no formula
$\varphi(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ and sequences of tuples $(\bar{a}_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$,
$(\bar{b}_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ in a model of $T$ such that $\varphi(\bar{a}_i, \bar{b}_j)$
holds if and only if $i \le j$. For a complete theory this is equivalent to $T$ being
$\kappa$-stable for some infinite cardinal $\kappa$.

Finite fields are excluded because every finite structure has a stable theory but a finite field
is not separably closed. The converse of the conjecture is a theorem of Wood: every separably
closed field has a stable theory.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)`, with variables split as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n`, has the *order property* in
the theory `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)ᵢ`, `(bⱼ)ⱼ` of tuples
in `M` indexed by `ℕ` such that `φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` holds in `M` if and only if `i ≤ j`.

The models are taken in `Type (max u v)`, as in `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`;
by the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this does not change the notion.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib/ModelTheory and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for `stable`, `order property`, `NIP`, `independence property`: nothing exists. Closest related API is `Theory.IsSatisfiable`/`Theory.ModelType` (used for the universe convention) and `Theory.Categorical`.
justification.name: StableFieldConjecture.HasOrderProperty
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no order property / stability for first-order theories. Defines: a formula `φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)` has the order property in `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` (in universe `max u v`, as in Mathlib's `Theory.IsSatisfiable`) and sequences `a b : ℕ → tuples in M` with `φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j` for all `i j` — exactly the Wikipedia (Stable theory) definition.

blocks.name: HasOrderProperty
blocks.text:
/-- A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)`, with variables split as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n`, has the *order property* in
the theory `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)ᵢ`, `(bⱼ)ⱼ` of tuples
in `M` indexed by `ℕ` such that `φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` holds in `M` if and only if `i ≤ j`.

The models are taken in `Type (max u v)`, as in `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`;
by the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this does not change the notion. -/
def HasOrderProperty (T : L.Theory) {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (a : ℕ → Fin m → M) (b : ℕ → Fin n → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

blocks.code:
def IsStable (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)), ¬ HasOrderProperty T φ
blocks.docstring: A theory `T` is *stable* if no formula has the order property in `T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No stability notion in Mathlib or the repo; `Theory.IsComplete`, `Theory.Categorical` are the nearest theory-level predicates but are unrelated.
justification.name: StableFieldConjecture.IsStable
justification.why_needed: Stability of a theory `T`: no formula `φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)` (any `m n`) has the order property in `T`. Applied to `Language.ring.completeTheory K`, which is complete, so it matches the Wikipedia definition for complete theories.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStable_completeTheory_of_finite (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] [Nonempty M] [Finite M] :
    IsStable (L.completeTheory M) := by
  rintro m n φ ⟨N, a, b, hab⟩
  have hN : Finite N := by
    have h := (realize_iff_of_model_completeTheory M N
      (Sentence.cardGe L (Nat.card M + 1)).not).2
    simp only [Sentence.realize_not, Sentence.realize_cardGe, not_le] at h
    have h' := h (by rw [← Nat.cast_card]; exact_mod_cast lt_add_one _)
    exact Cardinal.lt_aleph0_iff_finite.1 (h'.trans Cardinal.natCast_lt_aleph0)
  have ha : Function.Injective a := by
    intro i j hij
    by_contra hne
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h | h
    · have h1 := (hab i i).2 le_rfl
      rw [hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab j i).1 h1) (not_le.2 h)
    · have h1 := (hab j j).2 le_rfl
      rw [← hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab i j).1 h1) (not_le.2 h)
  exact not_injective_infinite_finite a ha

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every infinite field K, if the complete theory Th(K) in the language of rings is stable (no formula has the order property, equivalently κ-stable for some infinite κ), then K is separably closed (Mathlib `IsSepClosed`); Mathlib lacks a stability definition so it must be introduced, and the known converse (Wood) and the solved superstable case (Macintyre, Cherlin–Shelah) are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c03's declarations (HasOrderProperty / IsStable for a theory via ℕ-indexed half-graphs in a model, [CompatibleRing K] hypothesis, conclusion IsSepClosed K, DLO test) are a literal rendering of the Wikipedia definition and compile cleanly. Edits: merged the module/theorem docstrings of c06/c08 (explain Th(K) in the ring language, why Infinite is needed, universe convention), and added a proved @[category API] lemma `isStable_completeTheory_of_finite` (finite structures have stable theory), adapting c07's finite-structure lemma to the theory-level definition, to satisfy CONTRIBUTING.md's request for API tests of bespoke definitions.

context:
In the mathematical field of model theory, a theory  is called stable  if it satisfies certain combinatorial restrictions on its complexity. Stable theories are rooted in the proof of Morley's categoricity theorem and were extensively studied as part of Saharon Shelah's classification theory, which showed a dichotomy that either the models of a theory admit a nice classification or the models are too numerous to have any hope of a reasonable classification. A first step of this program was showing that if a theory is not stable then its models are too numerous to classify.
Stable theories were the predominant subject of pure model theory from the 1970s through the 1990s, so their study shaped modern model theory and there is a rich framework and set of tools to analyze them. A major direction in model theory is "neostability theory," which tries to generalize the concepts of stability theory to broader contexts, such as simple and NIP theories.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement; the notes correctly identify that stability must be introduced and that the converse and superstable case are out of scope.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field with a stable first-order theory
is separably closed. Here the first-order theory of a field $K$ is its complete theory
$\mathrm{Th}(K)$ in the language of rings $\{+, \cdot, -, 0, 1\}$.

Mathlib does not define stability of a first-order theory, so it is defined here. A theory $T$
is *stable* if no formula has the order property in $T$, i.e. there are no formula
$\varphi(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ and sequences of tuples $(\bar{a}_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$,
$(\bar{b}_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ in a model of $T$ such that $\varphi(\bar{a}_i, \bar{b}_j)$
holds if and only if $i \le j$. For a complete theory this is equivalent to $T$ being
$\kappa$-stable for some infinite cardinal $\kappa$.

Finite fields are excluded because every finite structure has a stable theory but a finite field
is not separably closed. The converse of the conjecture is a theorem of Wood: every separably
closed field has a stable theory.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder Language

universe u v

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)`, with variables split as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n`, has the *order property* in
the theory `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)ᵢ`, `(bⱼ)ⱼ` of tuples
in `M` indexed by `ℕ` such that `φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` holds in `M` if and only if `i ≤ j`.

The models are taken in `Type (max u v)`, as in `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsSatisfiable`;
by the downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem this does not change the notion. -/
def HasOrderProperty (T : L.Theory) {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (a : ℕ → Fin m → M) (b : ℕ → Fin n → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A theory `T` is *stable* if no formula has the order property in `T`. -/
def IsStable (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)), ¬ HasOrderProperty T φ

/-- The complete theory of a finite structure is stable. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStable_completeTheory_of_finite (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] [Nonempty M] [Finite M] :
    IsStable (L.completeTheory M) := by
  rintro m n φ ⟨N, a, b, hab⟩
  have hN : Finite N := by
    have h := (realize_iff_of_model_completeTheory M N
      (Sentence.cardGe L (Nat.card M + 1)).not).2
    simp only [Sentence.realize_not, Sentence.realize_cardGe, not_le] at h
    have h' := h (by rw [← Nat.cast_card]; exact_mod_cast lt_add_one _)
    exact Cardinal.lt_aleph0_iff_finite.1 (h'.trans Cardinal.natCast_lt_aleph0)
  have ha : Function.Injective a := by
    intro i j hij
    by_contra hne
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h | h
    · have h1 := (hab i i).2 le_rfl
      rw [hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab j i).1 h1) (not_le.2 h)
    · have h1 := (hab j j).2 le_rfl
      rw [← hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab i j).1 h1) (not_le.2 h)
  exact not_injective_infinite_finite a ha

/-- The theory of dense linear orders without endpoints is not stable: the formula `x ≤ y` has
the order property, witnessed in `ℚ`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStable_dlo : ¬ IsStable Language.order.dlo := by
  letI := orderStructure ℚ
  intro h
  refine h (leSymb.formula₂ (var (Sum.inl 0)) (var (Sum.inr 0)) :
    Language.order.Formula (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1)) ?_
  refine ⟨Theory.ModelType.of _ ℚ, fun i _ => (i : ℚ), fun j _ => (j : ℚ), fun i j => ?_⟩
  simp

/--
**Stable field conjecture.** Every infinite field $K$ whose complete first-order theory
$\mathrm{Th}(K)$ in the language of rings is stable is separably closed.

The hypothesis `CompatibleRing K` equips `K` with its `Language.ring`-structure in which the
symbols are interpreted by the field operations; every field admits such a structure
(`FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing`). The field must be infinite: finite fields have a
stable theory but are not separably closed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [Infinite K] [Ring.CompatibleRing K]
    (hK : IsStable (Language.ring.completeTheory K)) : IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture

items: Stability is formalized via the order-property characterization (Wikipedia: 'A common alternate definition of stable theories is that they do not have the order property'), not via counting types (κ-stable for some infinite κ); these are classically equivalent, and the order property is far simpler to state with Mathlib's existing `Formula.Realize` API.

The order property is stated at the level of the theory `Th(K)` ('some model of T'), not inside `K` itself; this matches the source ('field with a stable first-order theory') and avoids the known discrepancy where a structure can lack infinite half-graphs while its theory still has the order property.

The witness model in `HasOrderProperty` is taken in universe `max u v` (so `Type 0` for the ring language), following Mathlib's `Theory.IsSatisfiable` convention; by downward Löwenheim–Skolem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.

The first-order theory of `K` is `Language.ring.completeTheory K` under the hypothesis `[Ring.CompatibleRing K]`, Mathlib's recommended pattern; since the ring language has exactly the five function symbols and no relations, `CompatibleRing` forces the structure to be the field's own operations, so this is Th(K) in the language of rings.
Tuples of variables are encoded as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n` with `Sum.elim`, sequences are indexed by `ℕ`, and the half-graph condition is `i ≤ j`, exactly as in the Wikipedia text.

`Infinite K` is required as in the statement (finite fields are stable but not separably closed); `IsSepClosed` is Mathlib's class. Only the forward implication is stated; Wood's converse and the superstable (Macintyre, Cherlin–Shelah) case are not included, per the decomposition notes.

The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (the harness reads a single file); a proved `category test` declaration `not_isStable_dlo` (DLO is unstable, witnessed in ℚ) is included as the basic API test required by CONTRIBUTING.md for bespoke definitions.

references.title: Model theoretic stability and definability of types, after A. Grothendieck

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates are mathematically faithful; no candidate omitted the slot. Differences: (1) stability encoded as an ℕ-indexed half-graph in some model of Th(K) restricted to Type 0 (c02,c03,c04,c06,c08) vs. arbitrarily large finite half-graphs in K itself (c01,c05,c07) — equivalent by compactness/completeness of Th(K) and downward Löwenheim–Skolem for the countable ring language; the Type-0 restriction is non-vacuous since completeTheory.isSatisfiable gives such models. (2) c01/c02/c04/c05 supply the ring-language structure with `compatibleRingOfRing` inside the statement (via `let`/`@`), which is legal but less idiomatic than the `[CompatibleRing K]` hypothesis of c03/c06/c07/c08 (Mathlib's recommended pattern; every field admits such an instance, and it forces the symbols to be the field operations). Boundary checks: Fin 0 tuples cannot witness a half-graph (a₀ = a₁ forces φ(a₀,b₀) ↔ 0 ≤ 0 and ↔ 1 ≤ 0 simultaneously), `i ≤ j` vs `i < j` conventions are equivalent, parameter-free formulas suffice since parameters can be absorbed into ȳ. The known converse (Wood) and the superstable case are mentioned only in the module docstring as context, not stated. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; the one >100-char line is a reference URL, matching many existing Wikipedia files.
statement: The stable field conjecture: every infinite field with a stable first-order theory is separably closed.
